# Drawer

A panel that slides in from the side for a short task or a list of links, while the page stays in view behind it.

## Usage

```jsx
import { Button, Drawer, DrawerTrigger, Input } from "naksha";

<DrawerTrigger>
  <Button variant="primary">New project</Button>
  <Drawer
    title="New project"
    footer={(close) => (
      <>
        <Button onPress={close}>Cancel</Button>
        <Button variant="primary" onPress={() => { create(); close(); }}>Create project</Button>
      </>
    )}
  >
    <Input label="Project name" description="You can rename it later." />
  </Drawer>
</DrawerTrigger>

<Drawer title="Index" side="start" isDismissable isOpen={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  {links}
</Drawer>
```

| Prop | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | what the drawer holds, as a name | |
| `children` | the task or the list; a string becomes one paragraph | |
| `footer` | the actions, or a function that gets `close` | none |
| `isOpen`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | without a `DrawerTrigger` | |
| `side` | `start` or `end`: the edge it slides in from | `end` |
| `isDismissable` | a click outside closes it | `false` |

## Best practices

- Use a Drawer for a short task that needs the page as context (create a project, set filters) or for a list of places to go (an index). For one decision, use a Modal. For a long form, give it its own page.
- `end` for tasks, `start` for navigation, so a list of places opens from the same side as the page's reading order.
- Turn on `isDismissable` for a list of links. Leave it off for a form, so a stray click does not throw away what was typed.
- No drawer from a drawer, and no modal from a drawer.

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title "New project", actions "Cancel" / "Create project" | Title "Create a new project", actions "OK" / "Cancel" |
| A list of five links in an index drawer | The whole site map |

## Content

The title names what is inside in sentence case, with no question mark: a drawer holds a task or a list, not a question. Actions are verbs, secondary first, primary last.

## Anatomy and spacing

Modal's head and foot: header 24 / 16 / 0 / 24 with the title at 22, weight 600, and a small ghost close button; body 12 / 24 / 24, in the default text colour, and it scrolls on its own while the head and foot stay put; footer 16 / 24 on `bg-subtle` with a hairline above. The panel is 400 wide and the full height of the window, on `bg-raised` with `shadow-overlay`, a hairline on the edge that faces the page, and `overlay-scrim` over the rest. Below 600 wide it takes the whole width. Corners 0.

## States

Slides in from its edge over 280ms (`dur-overlay`, `ease-out`) while the scrim fades in; slides out in 200ms. Under reduced motion it only fades. In a right-to-left page `end` is the left edge, and it slides from there.

## Accessibility

**What Naksha provides.** The same React Aria ModalOverlay, Modal and Dialog as Modal: a `dialog` named by its title, focus moves in on open and cannot Tab out, the page behind is hidden from screen readers and cannot scroll, Escape closes, and focus returns to the trigger.

**What the designer decides.** Which side, whether a click outside closes it, and whether the task is short enough for a drawer.

**What the developer must not break.** Keep the close button and Escape working. Keep the title: it is the dialog's name.
